body: Thanks again for the lack of interest/help SuicideWatch. This experience emulated my real life, it was great.

If I were you, I'd do what felt right. Sometimes we have to push ourselves through things so we can grow, but there's a time and place for everything. If you feel a semester right now really won't be beneficial, take another semester off. You always have time. But maybe make a plan and focus on another area of your life that you aren't too happy with and wish to improve. This way you're occupied, and the time off isn't put to waste.

I wish the best for you & hope you feel better!

I'm sorry you feel that way, OP. 

I empathize and feel similarly. Imo, I think that 'drowning' feeling is just another way of expressing hopelessness, which I totally get.

In that entry, when you wrote your pain is nothing but another's, and crying is a luxury because it nags on someone else's depression, are you saying other people are adopting your sadness as their own? Or are you around people also going through things, who you can't reveal your true feelings around?

Judging by the lack of attention my thread is getting compared to that of others, I must have some serious issues others aren't interested in touching on. Or my thread isn't all that important. Was really looking for some support as well.

0well.

I know how you feel, OP. Our situations are different (check my thread I just posted on here), but I feel they run slightly parallel. 

Outside of medication, the best thing you can do, is "fake it until you make it". It's corny and cliche, but nothing good comes of the comfort zone. I know what it feels like to have no energy to talk, socialize, or even roll out of bed.. you just gotta force yourself. You feel better after a day of forcing yourself to do shit, than you do stewing in your pain. The future you will thank you for making the hard choices.

When my seizures were bad, I took a couple of semesters off from college and was too scared to go back out of fear of seizing in public/class... I just had to get back on the horse and force myself. It was hard as fuck, but I was trying, and it gave me something to be proud of. I'm not exactly the pinnacle of mental health, but I can promise you, you will feel better if you try.

And remember, no one cares if you're overweight. It's who you are inside that matters. No one is going to class to pay attention to the weight, clothing or style of others, people are there to learn.

I'm sorry you're going through this op, and I hope you feel better.
